-78.80060,35.90160.name: Atlantic Reproductive Medicine Specialists, PA
-78.80060,35.90160.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Susannah D. Copland, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

47.48849,42.97796.name: Центр репродукции и планировании детей
47.48849,42.97796.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

1.15102,49.02689.name: Charles River Laboratories Evreux
1.15102,49.02689.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of A Charles River Company. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-40.29630,-20.30917.name: Jules White Medicina Reprodutiva
-40.29630,-20.30917.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.juleswhite.com.br. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-73.99000,40.74400.name: Kindbody
-73.99000,40.74400.desc: A fertility company selling directly to employers as a staff benefit rather than to patients. Routing fertility treatment through an employment package means an employer chooses the provider, the clinical options and the coverage limits for its staff — a purchasing arrangement with no equivalent in most of medicine, and one that ties a reproductive decision to a job.

-84.54600,42.73200.name: Neogen
-84.54600,42.73200.desc: Supplies food safety testing including strip tests for engineered material, used at grain elevators and processing plants to accept or reject a load in minutes. Rapid tests are where a labelling threshold meets a lorry: the decision is made on the spot by a technician with a disposable device, and everything downstream follows from it.

-117.24000,32.88900.name: Alexandria Real Estate Equities
-117.24000,32.88900.desc: Owns and leases much of the purpose-built laboratory space in Cambridge, South San Francisco and San Diego. Biological work needs containment-rated buildings that take years to construct, so a landlord holding the supply in three clusters has a quiet say in which companies can exist at all.

10.52570,52.25990.name: Leibniz Institute DSMZ
10.52570,52.25990.desc: The German national collection of microorganisms and cell cultures, and the European counterpart to the American reference collection: it authenticates and holds strains for the long term rather than circulating engineered constructs. Its position in Europe also puts it inside the access and benefit-sharing rules that govern where a strain came from and who is owed what for it — a question the crop side of this map asks constantly about germplasm and the microbial side rarely asks at all.
